default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-288.title: Intraday trendline touch hold
E-288.hypothesis: A rising line through the session's last two higher swing lows (falling line through two lower swing highs) is drawn by chart traders who rest buy (sell) orders on it; the first touch that closes back on the trend side shows those orders absorbing the pullback, so trade the hold; a close through the line voids it.

E-289.title: Williams VIX-fix fear/greed spike reversal
E-289.hypothesis: Larry Williams' synthetic VIX (drop of the low from the window's highest close) spiking far above its 20-session norm marks forced, fearful selling; once the spike stops growing and a bar closes above the previous bar's high, the panic sellers are done and liquidity providers who bought from them lift the price (mirror: a greed spike from the lowest close).

E-290.title: Time-symmetric correction completion
E-290.hypothesis: After a leg larger than usual, a pullback that has lasted about half the leg's duration and retraced 20-80% of it without breaking down is a routine correction where the leg's holders did not exit; the first close beyond the previous bar's extreme at that time-symmetric point signals the correctors are done, so follow the leg.

E-291.title: Keltner-band walk exhaustion
E-291.hypothesis: Several consecutive closes outside an EMA +/- ATR Keltner band are a one-sided chase by late momentum traders; the first close back inside the band shows the chase has run out of new buyers (sellers) and their positions unwind toward the mean, so fade the re-entry.

E-292.title: VWAP-hug release follow
E-292.hypothesis: When every close of a window stays within a small distance of the session VWAP, benchmark-tracking execution dominates and no side has an edge; a close far beyond that hug band means a participant stopped tracking the benchmark and is demanding liquidity, and the VWAP traders who were pinned there re-hedge in the same direction; follow the release.

E-293.title: Order-block retest hold
E-293.hypothesis: The last opposite-colour bar before an impulse bar is where the impulsive participant started filling; when price first returns to that bar's range and closes back beyond it in the impulse direction, the unfilled remainder of that order defends the zone, so trade with the impulse; a close through the zone or a long wait voids it.

E-294.title: Heavy-volume takeover bar
E-294.hypothesis: Two consecutive bars both on abnormal volume for their minute, of opposite colour, where the second trades even more and closes beyond the first bar's open: the second side met the first side's heavy flow head-on and won; the losers of that contest exit over the next bars, so follow the second bar.

E-295.title: Higher-timeframe structure low test
E-295.hypothesis: When the last two completed 30-90 minute blocks of the session made a higher high and a higher low, swing traders reading that larger chart buy at the last block's low; a 1-5 minute bar that tests that low and closes up on the right side is their support holding, so trade with the larger structure (mirror for lower highs).

E-296.title: Close-location churn fade
E-296.hypothesis: Several consecutive bars that all close near their highs while the price makes no net progress mean buyers lift every bar into its close but a larger passive seller sells each new bar back down; the aggressive side is spending effort for no result and gives up, so fade it (mirror for closes near the lows).

E-297.title: Fractal break while the Alligator sleeps
E-297.hypothesis: Bill Williams' Alligator lines (smoothed medians 13/8/5, shifted) bunched together mean the market is asleep and stops cluster just beyond the last confirmed fractal high/low; the first close through a fractal while the lines are still tangled is the start of a new swing that wakes trend traders, so follow it only out of the sleeping state.
